header.title: Desktop is solid, mobile leaks conversions
header.subtitle: The messaging and structure are decent overall, but mobile layout and CTA visibility create avoidable friction on first screen.

summary_panel.one_liner: This page is close on desktop, but mobile users have to scroll through too much content before they understand the offer and find the primary action.
top_3_problems: Mobile hero pushes CTA below the fold
Headline and subheadline stack into a dense mobile block
Sticky elements and popups compete for viewport space on mobile
summary_panel.cta_hint: You likely have more upside from mobile layout fixes than another headline rewrite.

issue_cards.title: Primary CTA is not visible quickly on mobile
issue_cards.problem: On mobile, the hero stack (announcement bar, headline, subheadline, image, badges) pushes the primary CTA below the initial viewport.
issue_cards.why_it_hurts: Users cannot act when intent is highest, which reduces tap-through and increases early drop-off.

evidence.value: Primary CTA appears below initial mobile viewport without scrolling
Top-of-page utility bar consumes vertical space before hero content

issue_cards.fix: Reduce first-screen height and move a clear primary CTA higher, or add a sticky mobile CTA after initial scroll.

issue_cards.title: Mobile first screen contains too many competing elements
issue_cards.problem: Multiple badges, trust chips, and visual modules compete with the main message before the user understands the page.
issue_cards.why_it_hurts: Crowded first screens slow comprehension and reduce the chance that users reach the intended CTA with confidence.

evidence.value: Hero includes stacked chips/badges and a large visual before CTA on mobile

issue_cards.fix: Trim non-essential hero elements on mobile and keep one proof cue plus the CTA above the fold.

issue_cards.title: Good headline becomes hard to scan when wrapped on mobile
issue_cards.problem: The headline likely works on desktop, but line breaks and adjacent copy create a heavy text block on smaller screens.
issue_cards.why_it_hurts: Mobile users scan in shorter bursts; dense hero text reduces immediate understanding and action confidence.

evidence.value: Close your books in half the time with automated reconciliation
Headline/subheadline wrap into a dense multi-line stack on mobile

issue_cards.fix: Shorten the mobile headline variant or trim the subheadline so the key outcome is visible in 2-3 lines.
issue_cards.example_rewrite: Close your books faster with automated reconciliation

issue_cards.title: Secondary actions compete with the primary mobile CTA
issue_cards.problem: Secondary links and utility actions appear prominent enough on mobile to distract from the main conversion path.
issue_cards.why_it_hurts: Mobile attention is narrower; competing actions pull taps away from the primary conversion event.

evidence.value: Multiple buttons/links in hero/navigation area compete visually on mobile

issue_cards.fix: Visually prioritize one primary action on mobile and demote secondary actions to text links or lower placement.

issue_cards.title: Mobile users may miss reassurance copy before tapping
issue_cards.problem: Risk-reducing details (trial terms, integrations, data security notes) appear later, which matters more on mobile where scroll depth is lower.
issue_cards.why_it_hurts: Users who need one reassurance cue may abandon before reaching deeper sections.

evidence.value: Reassurance content appears below multiple product/feature sections on mobile

issue_cards.fix: Bring one concise reassurance line (e.g., no credit card, quick setup, secure integrations) closer to the mobile CTA.

items.note: Offer is mostly clear, though mobile presentation delays clarity.
Audience is reasonably clear in copy and examples.
Headline is strong on desktop but less effective when wrapped on mobile.
CTA wording is decent, but visibility and competition reduce mobile effectiveness.
Differentiation is present but not the primary bottleneck compared with mobile UX.
Proof appears credible, but some signals may sit too low for mobile users.
Desktop structure is acceptable, but mobile first-screen hierarchy is overloaded.
Reassurance exists but arrives late in the mobile journey.
CTA placement, density, and competing elements create a clear mobile conversion drag.

quick_wins_section.title: Quick Wins
quick_wins_section.subtitle: Mobile-first fixes (fast)
items: Reduce mobile hero height so the primary CTA appears in the first viewport.
Remove or collapse non-essential hero badges/chips on mobile.
Trim the mobile subheadline to 1-2 lines and keep the key outcome first.
Demote secondary actions in the mobile hero/nav.
Add one short reassurance line directly under the mobile CTA.
